language.script_notes: Romanian with ș and ț; bilingual Romanian–Hungarian signs are common in the Székely counties of the center-east, with Hungarian letters ő and ű, and German-language signs and names survive in old Saxon towns such as Sibiu and Brașov.

road_furniture.guardrail_type: As national, with more guardrails on winding mountain roads.
road_furniture.curb_style: As national; cobbled town centers with Saxon and Habsburg buildings.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: As national — holey poles with white-painted bases and thick black-backed warning triangles.

architecture.roof_style: Steep red or orange clay tile roofs with dormers on Saxon houses; tall shingled or wooden roofs and steeples on mountain churches.
architecture.roof_material: Red clay tile is specific to the area, alongside wood shingle in the mountains.
architecture.wall_construction: Villages of Saxon rowhouses with courtyard gates set gable-end to the road, each centered on a fortified church with defensive walls and towers (over 150 survive, and seven villages are UNESCO-listed); carved wooden gates and wooden churches in the northern highlands; Habsburg-era towns with pastel baroque facades.
architecture.wall_color_palette: White walls with red tile roofs, and pastel baroque plaster in the towns.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Fortified Saxon churches surrounded by walls; brightly painted Baroque town squares in Sibiu and Brașov; Bran-style hilltop castles; carved wooden gates and shingle-roofed churches; haystacks and shepherd huts on the high pastures.

nature.vegetation: Dense spruce and beech forest, alpine meadows above the tree line, hay meadows dotted with haystacks, and orchards and vineyards on the hill slopes.
nature.terrain: A rolling plateau enclosed by the high arc of the Carpathian Mountains, with peaks over 2,500m, deep valleys, gorges and mountain passes.
nature.climate_signature: Cooler and wetter than the plains, with snowy mountain winters and misty green hills.

vehicles.plate_color: As national — county codes such as CJ (Cluj), SB (Sibiu), BV (Brașov).
vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: Dacia dominates; horse-drawn carts are still used in villages, and hay wagons in summer.

google_coverage.coverage_notes: Dense coverage of towns, villages and the main mountain roads.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Bilingual Hungarian signs and towns in the center, plus similar baroque architecture
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Letters Ș and Ț, holey poles with white bases and thick black-backed warning triangles are found here; Hungarian language dominates only in the Székely enclaves.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Shared Carpathian mountain villages and wooden church traditions
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Slovak black bollards with double reflectors and Ukrainian Cyrillic are absent; the Romanian holey pole and comma-below letters appear here.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Same country, same national road furniture and plates
confusion_set.tiebreaker: The center is mountainous and wooded with Saxon villages and red tile roofs; the south and east are flat farmland with metal roofs and Orthodox churches.
